name: OpenFlux
description: Network stack research tool. TCP tunnel with pluggable transports.
one_liner: A technical networking tool for building custom, hard-to-detect internet tunnels — the kind of thing used to get around network blocks or restrictions.
buyer: No legitimate mainstream buyer — the project's own README explicitly disclaims commercial use and censorship-circumvention intent, which makes it a poor foundation for an above-board business.
business_use_cases: A network security researcher could reference the code when studying tunneling/detection techniques for defensive research.
A commercial VPN provider could theoretically study the pluggable-transport approach for their own product's engineering, without using this project directly.
None of these are businesses built on this repo itself — it's research-grade infrastructure, not a product.

money_ideas.idea: There isn't an honest, low-risk money idea here — commercial products in this space (VPNs) require licensing, legal review, and jurisdiction-aware compliance well beyond this repo.

steal_this: Skip this one for a weekend business — it's explicitly non-commercial research tooling with real legal and platform-policy risk attached to its actual use case.
